questions.question: You have 3 red beads and 5 blue beads. Is the total number of beads even or odd?
questions.explain: 3 is odd and 5 is odd. When you add two odd numbers, the sum is always even. So 3 + 5 makes an even number.

questions.question: You have 7 yellow marbles and 9 white marbles. Is the total number of marbles even or odd?
questions.explain: 7 is odd and 9 is odd. Two odd numbers always add to make an even number. So 7 + 9 is even.

questions.question: A bag has 12 red sweets and 8 blue sweets. Is the total number of sweets even or odd?
questions.explain: 12 is even and 8 is even. Two even numbers always add to make an even number. So 12 + 8 is even.

questions.question: Sara has 35 stickers. She gets 7 more from a book. Is her new total even or odd?
questions.explain: 35 is odd and 7 is odd. Two odd numbers always add to make an even number. So 35 + 7 is even.

questions.question: Which pair of numbers always makes an odd sum?
questions.explain: An even number plus an odd number always gives an odd sum. 4 is even and 9 is odd, so 4 + 9 is always odd.

questions.question: Jai says 7 + 9 is odd. He says this because 7 and 9 are both odd. Is Jai right?
questions.explain: Jai is wrong. Two odd numbers always add to make an even number. So 7 + 9 = 16, which is even.

questions.question: Leo puts 5 red cubes and 5 blue cubes in one box. He tries to pair them all up. Is the total even or odd?
options: Odd, one cube has no pair
questions.explain: 5 + 5 = 10, and 10 cubes make 5 full pairs with none left, so the total is even. Two odd numbers always add up to an even number.

questions.question: A plate has 18 crackers. Dad puts 7 more on it. Is the number of crackers even or odd?
questions.explain: 18 + 7 = 25, and when you pair 25 crackers up, one cracker has no partner, so the total is odd. An even number plus an odd number is always odd.

questions.question: Mia has 13 buttons. Raj has 5 buttons. They put them together and share them into two equal piles. Does it work?
questions.explain: 13 + 5 = 18, and 18 splits into 9 and 9 with nothing left, so the total is even. Two odd numbers always make an even sum.

questions.question: Nina has 6 shells. Her gran gives her 8 more. Can she put them all in pairs with none left?
questions.explain: 6 + 8 = 14, and 14 shells make 7 pairs with none left over, so the sum is even. Two even numbers always give an even sum.

questions.question: Ravi picks 15 blueberries. His sister picks 19. Will the total be even or odd?
options: Odd, one berry has no pair
questions.explain: 15 + 19 = 34, and 34 berries make 17 pairs with none left, so the sum is even. The common trap is thinking odd plus odd stays odd.

questions.question: Mia wants to know if 28 + 35 is even or odd. She does not want to add them. What should she check?
options: The first digit of the sum
questions.explain: Look at each number first: 28 is even and 35 is odd, so the sum must be odd. The first digit of a number never tells you if it is even or odd.

questions.question: The gym has 18 chairs. A teacher brings in 9 more. Is the number of chairs even or odd?
options: Odd, even plus odd is odd
questions.explain: 18 is even and 9 is odd, so one chair is left with no partner: 27 is odd. Do not judge by the first digit, because 27 starts with 2 but is still odd.

questions.question: Jon collects 16 acorns. He finds 14 more under a tree. Is his total even or odd?
options: Odd, one acorn is left out
questions.explain: 16 and 14 are both even, so every acorn finds a pair: 30 is even. The first digit 3 does not decide, and a total ending in 0 is even too.

questions.question: Ivan has 11 cards. Ava gives him 5 cards, then Ben gives him 2. Is his total even or odd?
options: Odd, odd plus odd is odd
questions.explain: 11 + 5 = 16, and 16 + 2 = 18, which makes 9 pairs with none left. Two odd numbers give an even sum, and adding an even number keeps it even.

questions.question: Sam has 13 pine cones. He wants an even number in all. Which number should he add?
questions.explain: 13 is odd, so he needs another odd number: 13 + 9 = 22, which makes 11 pairs. Adding an even number to 13 would leave the total odd.

questions.question: A party has 17 girls and 13 boys. Then 2 more boys come in. Every child needs a partner, so will one be left out?
questions.explain: 17 + 13 = 30 and 30 + 2 = 32, so the children make 16 full pairs. Two odd numbers add to an even number, and adding 2 keeps it even.

questions.question: Ben works out 12 + 6 = 18. He says 18 is odd because it starts with a 1. What went wrong?
options: He should use the last digit
questions.explain: Even or odd comes from the last digit, not the first one. 18 ends in 8 and makes 9 pairs, so the sum of two even numbers is even.
